headline: Google Gemini Notebook Gets a Major Upgrade: Here’s What’s New
snippet: Google announced new features for Gemini Notebook, the AI-powered research and study tool previously known as NotebookLM. The update introduces real-time voice conversations, an audio recorder and interactive learning tools such as quizzes and flashcards. The company is also offering eligible college students free access to its paid Google AI plans for one year, with higher usage limits in Gemini Notebook. Real-Time Voice Chats Gemini Notebook will soon let users have real-time spoken conversations with their notebooks through its mobile app on Android, iPhone, and iPad. Google says the feature will work in nearly 100 languages. Users will be able to ask questions, get step-by-step guidance and interrupt the conversation while speaking. Responses will remain grounded in the sources added to the notebook, letting users discuss study material through voice instead of typing questions and reading text responses. The feature is rolling out to Google AI Ultra subscribers aged 18 and above this week, with Google AI Pro subscribers and other users set to get access soon. Audio Recording Google is also adding an audio recorder to the Gemini Notebook mobile app starting next week. Users can record lectures, meetings or their own thoughts directly inside the app. The recordings will become sources in the relevant notebook, alongside documents, handwritten notes, worksheets and photos. Users can then chat with, cite and build from these recordings while continuing to edit their notes. Interactive Study Tools Gemini Notebook is adding interactive learning overviews under Reports, combining summaries with studio content such as infographics, quizzes and flashcards. New quiz formats will include short-answer, multiple-select and fill-in-the-blank questions. Users will also be able to review their quiz and flashcard performance through notebook chat and customise questions. Short Video Overviews are expanding to more than 80 languages, with videos of around 60 seconds combining narration and educational animations. Also Read: Google Gemini Notebook’s New Upgrade Could Change How You Study Free Google AI Pro for Students Eligible college students in the US can claim one year of Google AI Pro for free, normally priced at USD 19.99 per month. The offer provides 4x higher usage limits in Gemini Notebook. Eligible college students in more than 140 markets outside the US can receive Google AI Plus free for one year, with 2x higher usage limits. Both offers can be claimed until December 31, 2026, subject to Google's terms.

headline: Baqai Dental College students strengthen preventive dentistry skills through fluoride training
snippet: KARACHI: Strengthening preventive dentistry requires dental students to understand not only how oral diseases are treated, but also how evidence-based interventions can help prevent them. A Fluoride Gel Application Workshop at Baqai Dental College provided students with academic instruction and practical exposure to topical fluoride therapy, highlighting the role of fluoride in dental caries prevention and community oral healthcare. Organised by the Department of Community Dentistry, Baqai Dental College, the workshop focused on the scientific basis, indications and clinical application of fluoride gel as a professional preventive measure. Connecting dental education with preventive care The workshop was conducted under the guidance and supervision of Prof Dr Asghar Ali Shigri, Head of the Department of Community Dentistry, Baqai Dental College, with Dr Nauman, Dr Raza, Dr Mehwish and Dr Samreen serving as facilitators. The academic session examined the importance of fluoride in maintaining oral health and its role in the prevention and control of dental caries, one of the most common oral health problems affecting communities worldwide. The training placed preventive care alongside conventional clinical treatment, reinforcing the role of dentists in preventing oral disease, promoting healthy behaviours and educating individuals and communities about measures that can support long-term oral health. Understanding fluoride's role in protecting teeth During the workshop, Prof Dr Asghar Ali Shigri delivered an informative and interactive session explaining the mechanism of action of fluoride and its contribution to improving the resistance of tooth enamel against acid attacks. Students were introduced to the indications and benefits of topical fluoride therapy, with particular attention to fluoride gel application. The discussion connected the scientific principles of fluoride with its practical application, helping students understand the rationale behind professional topical fluoride use as part of a broader preventive dentistry approach. From classroom learning to clinical application A detailed demonstration gave students practical insight into the steps involved in fluoride gel application. The procedure covered patient preparation, selection and placement of appropriate trays, proper isolation and moisture control, application of fluoride gel, and precautions before, during and after the procedure. The facilitators emphasised the importance of following appropriate techniques and safety measures to support effective and suitable fluoride delivery. The practical component allowed students to observe the clinical application of concepts discussed during the workshop, strengthening the connection between theoretical knowledge and preventive dental practice. Preventive dentistry extends beyond disease treatment The facilitators also highlighted the importance of preventive dentistry in reducing the burden of oral diseases within the community. Students were encouraged to recognise that the role of dental professionals extends beyond treating established disease. Patient education, oral health promotion and appropriate preventive interventions are also important components of dental practice. This perspective is particularly relevant to dental caries, where prevention and risk reduction can complement treatment and help individuals maintain better oral health over time. Building skills for prevention-focused dental practice The interactive format encouraged students to actively participate in discussions and ask questions about fluoride therapy and its clinical application. The workshop further emphasised the importance of incorporating preventive strategies into routine dental practice. Fluoride gel application was discussed as a professional preventive measure when appropriately indicated, including for individuals who may have an increased risk of developing dental caries. The combination of academic discussion and practical demonstration gave students an opportunity to better understand how preventive concepts translate into clinical practice. Strengthening community dentistry education The workshop reflected the Department of Community Dentistry at Baqai Dental College's commitment to combining theoretical instruction with practical exposure and community-oriented preventive healthcare. Under the supervision of Prof Dr Asghar Ali Shigri and with the facilitation of Dr Nauman, Dr Raza, Dr Mehwish and Dr Samreen, the session brought together fluoride science, clinical technique and the broader principles of oral health promotion. By familiarising students with topical fluoride therapy and its preventive rationale, the workshop contributed to their academic and professional preparation for dentistry that places greater emphasis on disease prevention, patient education and community oral health. Ultimately, the training reinforced an important principle of preventive dentistry: effective oral healthcare is not limited to treating disease after it develops; prevention and education are fundamental to protecting long-term oral health.
